concern: The stock disconnect body destroys the reflash workqueue before disabling and freeing the IRQ; an in-flight IRQ/reset callback could appear to queue work into a destroyed queue.
evidence_chain: Stock Ghidra at 0x00112b04 confirms cancel_delayed_work_sync(TCM+0x3c8), flush and destroy of TCM+0x430, then IRQ disable callback and devm_free_irq. The 392-byte/98-instruction stock body remains retained under the exact symbol.

The stock reset callback at 0x00113a9c queues only the helper work item (TCM+0x528) on the helper queue (TCM+0x548). The helper worker is the producer that can schedule delayed reflash work on TCM+0x430.
The reconstructed reset callback and helper scheduling share syna_dev_helper_work_lock. syna_dev_helper_workqueue_stop detaches the helper queue under that lock, closing future admission.

syna_dev_remove calls helper_workqueue_stop, cancel_work_sync on TCM+0x528, flushes and destroys the helper queue before cdev removal reaches syna_dev_disconnect. The helper is therefore drained before the exact disconnect body cancels and destroys the reflash queue.

Probe rollback and connect-allocation rollback reach disconnect before probe allocates the helper queue. The TCM remove callback is invoked at the end of normal remove, after the same helper-stop/drain sequence.
conclusion: No use-after-destroy defect is established for the recovered module call paths. Keep the 392-byte stock disconnect body and current HARDENED_STOCK_DEVIATION classification unchanged; no source edit or canonical rebuild was warranted by this review.
limits: This is a static call-path and ordering review; IRQ/workqueue concurrency was not exercised on Android or NX809J hardware.
The conclusion applies to the enumerated recovered in-module paths; behavior of an external caller not represented in the module evidence is not proven.
